children: CHICAGO-McDonald's plans to invest billions of dollars to help its franchisees make investments in equipment and their operations to better compete with fast-food rivals.

The restaurant giant said Wednesday that it would spend around $8.5 billion to provide franchisees with rent assistance and help with capital improvements through 2036 as part of a new corporate strategy. The financial commitment, the company said, is in addition to its typical capital-spending plans.

Pillars of the company's strategy, known as Next, are around improving food taste and quality, the consumer experience, restaurant operations and hospitality. Executives introduced Next earlier this year and are expected to share more details on its plans at an investor event Wednesday.
"We must be the first choice for more customers more often," McDonald's Chief Executive Chris Kempczinski said during the event at the company's Chicago headquarters.

The planned investments come as McDonald's is working to boost its sales and profits from its operations. With franchisees running most of McDonald's restaurants worldwide, the restaurant chain's fortunes are linked to their ability to navigate pressures such as rising food and labor costs and consumers calling for more affordable products.
Kempczinski said that customer-traffic growth in its major markets is expected to be flat in coming years and that McDonald's needs to capture more share to increase sales.

McDonald's has said its restaurants need to improve food quality to get customers in the door. The company is testing hand-breaded chicken in the U.S. and has rolled out a new line of crafted sodas and energy drinks infused with Red Bull this year. Selling items like hand-breaded chicken would require many locations to add kitchen equipment and make changes in food-handling practices.
The company wants to increase its share in the global beverage and chicken markets by 1.5 percentage points by 2030, while maintaining its position as the biggest fast-food burger seller.

As part of its plans, the company also said it wants to introduce AI technology in restaurants to help boost returns. Among the tools under consideration are providing restaurant workers and managers with access to chatbots to answer questions, as well as testing voice-AI ordering at the drive-through.

McDonald's is also aiming to improve the service in its restaurants, making one of its biggest hospitality pushes in its history next month. The company said Wednesday that its "Make it Golden" improvement program will be a multiyear effort.
